answer: Physical Provenance Chain. Each agent identity must periodically present a copper token whose unique oxidation pattern is logged at a registered wharf upon receipt of shipped goods. The chain of custody, including each relic transported, is recorded as a hash sequence linking agent to prior handlers. An attacker duplicating identities must physically acquire and transport distinct copper tokens through real wharf logistics, incurring shipping, handling, and time costs per identity rather than a one-time payment.
